rows.question: What is LLM (Large Language Model)?
rows.output: A model trained on large amounts of text that generates text by predicting the tokens following its input. It can handle many tasks, including question answering, summarization, and code generation, simply by changing the instructions (prompt).

rows.question: Briefly explain Context window.
rows.output: The maximum total number of input and output tokens an LLM can handle in one call. Conversation history and tool results must also fit within this limit, making the choice of what to pass to the model important.

rows.question: What is Hallucination?
rows.output: The phenomenon of an LLM generating plausible content that is factually incorrect or nonexistent. It is more likely when asked about things the model does not know, such as recent information or organization- or course-specific details. Mitigations include consulting external data through tools, asking for evidence, and detecting errors through evaluation.

rows.question: What is LoRA?
rows.output: A PEFT method that freezes pretrained weights, represents weight updates as the product of two small matrices (low-rank matrices), and trains only those small matrices. It trains few parameters and saves the results (adapters) in small files. The Lecture 02 exercises cover LoRA.

rows.question: Briefly explain QLoRA.
rows.output: A method that saves memory by quantizing base-model weights to, for example, 4 bits, then trains with LoRA. This lets smaller GPUs handle larger models. In the Lecture 02 exercises, the model fits in GPU memory, so we train with LoRA and compare memory and output differences when loading in 4-bit in the advanced section.

rows.question: What is Overfitting?
rows.output: A state in which the model fits training data excessively and performs worse on unseen inputs. Detect it by measuring performance on validation data not used for training.

rows.question: What is MCP (Model Context Protocol)?
rows.output: An open standard protocol connecting AI applications to external tools and data sources. Tools exposed through an MCP server can be used in a common way from compatible agents and editors (MCP clients). In Lecture 05, you will experience this by turning glossary search into an MCP server.

rows.question: Briefly explain Guardrail.
rows.output: A constraint or check designed to prevent undesirable agent behavior or outputs. Methods include rules in instructions, restricting tool permissions, checking outputs, and requesting human confirmation before important operations.

rows.question: What is Harness?
rows.output: A program that surrounds an LLM with a loop, tools, a user interface (UI), and so on to enable actual work. Claude Code and Pi are examples. Pi is known as a thin harness with just four built-in tools: read, write, edit, and bash.

rows.question: What is Pi?
rows.output: An open-source (MIT-licensed) coding agent that runs in the terminal. It has minimal features and a minimal system prompt, designed for users to extend. Version 1.0 was released in October 2026. Its npm package name is @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent.

rows.question: What is Default model?
rows.output: The standard model for AIE2026 exercises and homework is gemini-3.5-flash-lite, chosen with free-tier rate limits and stable course operation in mind. You may switch models with the AIE_MODEL environment variable or use your own API subscription.

rows.question: Briefly explain answer.md.
rows.output: The file for recording exercise and homework results for each AIE2026 lecture. Located at lectures/NN/answer.md. Record the level attempted, what you did, results, and observations, then submit by opening a PR from your working branch to main in your own fork.

rows.question: What does HITL mean in agent design?
rows.output: Incorporating human confirmation or approval into agent processing. Used before operations that are difficult to undo, such as writing or sending data. In Pydantic AI, tools with requires_approval=True support this.

rows.question: In LoRA, what does the r hyperparameter control?
rows.output: A hyperparameter that determines the size of the low-rank matrices used in each prediction. A larger value increases expressive capacity, but also increases the number of trainable parameters and memory use.

rows.question: Why would I get a 429 error from an LLM API?
rows.output: That error means the model requested more tokens than available at the time. Too many requests or excessive usage within a given time period will cause it to call the server from a different address.

rows.question: What does Low-Rank Adaptation do to a pretrained model?
rows.output: A method of further training a pretrained model on small amounts of new data. It trains only a small subset of model parameters instead of all parameters, saving memory and computation. The same structure as LoRA uses two matrices to represent weight updates: one for the model and one for the loader.

rows.question: How do I pass a Codespaces secret to my code, and what if my Codespace is already running?
rows.output: Adding a secret to your Codespace configuration. For example, specify a GEMINI_API_KEY in your .codespace or commit it to your repository. If you add it as a environment variable, it will not be passed to your code.

rows.question: What goes into devcontainer.json?
rows.output: A configuration file listing the Python version, extensions, and startup commands for each development container. For this course, specify the course index as the Python version and adk web as the extension.

rows.question: What is instruction tuning?
rows.output: A method of further training a model using pairs of inputs and desired outputs, such as questions and model answers. A representative method for teaching instruction-following behavior.

rows.question: Walk me through the tool-calling loop of an agent.
rows.output:
A loop that runs multiple times until the model gives a final answer. In Pydantic AI, it looks like this:

```python
for iteration in range(5):
    input_text = user_question + "\n" + system_prompt + "\n\n"
    output = model.invoke(Toolname=input_text)
    result = parse_output(output)
    if result.is_final_answer or iteration > 3:
        break
    print(result)
```

This course uses `model.invoke()` for questions and `tool_calls` for commands. Both return a result with `is_final_answer` set to True after enough questions or tool calls.

rows.question: Which model do the AIE2026 exercises use by default?
rows.output: The AIE (Agent Development Kit) comes with pre-trained models built into Python. In this course, glossary search uses AI while implementing a loop in Python. Choosing a model with the same language capability as the tool is important when selecting an AI model.

rows.question: What should I avoid doing with my API key, and how is it read in this course?
rows.output: Do not commit your API key to version control. It is too likely to be recorded by another AI model. In this course, create a separate secret key in your own account settings and use it through the Agent → Tools section.

rows.question: Explain quantisation of model weights.
rows.output: A technique for representing model weights with fewer bits (for example, from 16 bits to 4 bits) to reduce memory use and computation. Accuracy may decrease slightly.

rows.question: Why do LLMs sometimes confidently make up facts?
rows.output: That is not something agents do. Their output is likely to be incorrect because they have not been trained to detect or cite incorrect information.

rows.question: How do I avoid name collisions between tools from multiple MCP servers?
rows.output: Adding a prefix such as server_name or source_file to distinguish identically named tools when using multiple MCP servers. This course's app/agent.py automatically adds the server name from the configuration (for example, glossary_search_glossary; Pydantic AI's load_mcp_toolsets does the same). More tools mean more descriptions sent to the model, affecting tool-selection accuracy and token counts.

rows.question: What is RAG (retrieval-augmented generation)?
rows.output: A method that retrieves relevant page snippets from a library or file system, passes them to an LLM, and then generates text based on the retrieved snippets. In this course, we use fetch to retrieve the course glossary from URLs and treat each URL as a separate retrieval call.

rows.question: Can you explain RLHF?
rows.output: A method that trains a model on pairs of inputs and desired outputs, such as questions and model answers. A representative method for teaching instruction-following behavior.

rows.question: What is a vector database used for?
rows.output: A system that stores models as vectors and searches using LLMs. It has little to no human interaction or configuration. The Lecture 02 exercises cover Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).

rows.question: What is an embedding in machine learning?
rows.output: A function that converts model outputs (scores or IDs) into human-readable text or numbers. This makes further processing easier. In Pydantic AI, it is provided by the TextModel.

rows.question: How does beam search decoding work?
rows.output: A method that repeatedly chooses the next token according to the probability of that token given the entire history of tokens and all emitted characters. It is suitable for tasks with many possible outputs, such as question answering and machine translation.

rows.question: What is knowledge distillation?
rows.output: A method of training with smaller models and evaluation with larger models. It is suitable when the same data and evaluation metrics do not distinguish the answers correctly or incorrectly.

rows.question: What is a Mixture of Experts model?
rows.output: A model that achieves state-of-the-art performance on many tasks by combining outputs from multiple experts. Each expert is trained on a slightly different dataset or format, allowing it to handle a different type of input or output. A representative is chosen by averaging the expert outputs. This can greatly improve performance on tasks suited to one expert but not another.

rows.question: What is prompt injection?
rows.output: A threat in which an attacker specifies the model to use, arguments, or output format by embedding it into the question or role definition. Since the model reads it as part of the prompt, it can influence behavior. Mitigations include separating configuration from source, checking limits, and detecting errors.

rows.question: What does top-p sampling do?
rows.output: A method that selects the top N most likely outputs for each input. This can make agent responses more consistent and predictable, though it may underfit when there are few options.

rows.question: What is chain-of-thought prompting?
rows.output: A method that encourages model step-by-step reasoning by asking questions or displaying intermediate results. It is suitable for teaching reasoning and debugging.
